## Findings outside the claims

**F1 — `src/core/types.ts:5-6`, `:162-164`, `:172-176` and `guides/csv.md:57-58`: the unit corrected one instance of a false attribution to `@orkestrel/database` and shipped the rest, leaving the same file self-contradictory.**

What is wrong: csv-subj-4 had the unit restate the `TableExport` interop claim, and `src/core/types.ts:286-292` now correctly reads "`@orkestrel/database` declares `TableDefinition { primary, columns, schema }`. This package's `Columns` map is structurally identical to that package's `ColumnMap`". Two declarations earlier, `src/core/types.ts:172-176` still reads "Structurally identical to `@orkestrel/database`'s `Columns` (never imported) … so an `export` round-trips through `import` on either package", and `:162-164` still reads "mirrors `@orkestrel/database`'s `ColumnType` structurally". The file header at `:4-8` still names "its `TableExport` shape". `guides/csv.md:57` and `:58` repeat both attributions in the Types table, two rows above the `TableExport` row the unit corrected at `:66`.

Why it matters: `ColumnType` and `Columns` are public exports, so these remarks ship inside `dist/src/core/index.d.ts` and reach every consumer. I verified the attributions independently: a grep for `ColumnType|\bColumns\b|TableExport` across `/home/user/fleet/database/src` returns **no matches at all**; that package declares `ColumnMap` at `/home/user/fleet/database/src/core/types.ts:438` and `TableDefinition` at `:570`. So three published sentences name types that do not exist, and the "round-trips through `import` on either package" clause is the same lossless-round-trip claim csv-subj-4 struck at `TableExport`. `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity requires a prose claim to be falsified the way a code claim is, and § Parity's closing rule requires the prose to be re-read against what actually shipped. The unit's own report discloses this as findings 1 and 2, which is correct conduct — but disclosure does not make the shipped bytes true, and the state the tip would be committed and packed in is one where the same table asserts a correct fact and a false one about the same sibling package.

What right looks like: in `src/core/types.ts:162-164` replace the `ColumnType` remark's attribution with what is true — the literal set is a portable storage-type vocabulary this package declares locally, and no `@orkestrel/database` type of that name exists. In `:172-176` replace the `Columns` remark with the same structural statement the `TableExport` remark now carries: `Columns` is structurally identical to `@orkestrel/database`'s `ColumnMap`, and delete the "round-trips through `import` on either package" clause. In `:4-8` replace "its `TableExport` shape" with "its `TableDefinition` shape". In `guides/csv.md:57` and `:58` restate the two Behavior cells the same way. Change no type and no runtime behaviour; this is a documentation repair of exactly the class csv-subj-4 already ruled on.
